author: resilience-lead (AI practice-lead agent). Advises; the product owner approves (gate RQ1).
ownerDecision: D3 accepted by the product owner on 27 Oct 2026: written ladder, the higher of the RTO and RPO rungs; DR-05 only for RTO under 15 minutes with near-zero RPO, shown beside DR-04 as a business choice; modifiers add controls, not rungs.
note: Replaces resilience-iq/design/decision-matrix.json (S1-S5, not read by the engine) and the pattern bonuses in runtime.ts:586-591. In RQ3 this file moves to resilience-iq/knowledge/ and becomes the only source of the recommended rung. Band edges are LTM judgements grounded in the provider guidance cited; each carries its basis and status. Claim ids are assigned in RQ2.

rungs.name: Backup and restore
rungs.definition: Data and configuration are backed up to a separate location; on disaster the infrastructure is redeployed (ideally from code), the application deployed and the data restored.

providerEquivalents.rpo: hours (point-in-time recovery can lower it to as low as 5 minutes in some cases)

providerEquivalents.note: Google gives no numeric bands; the mapping of cold to DR-01 is an LTM mapping.

providerEquivalents.pattern: Restore to a cold site or rebuilt infrastructure
providerEquivalents.note: NIST SP 800-34 Rev. 1 describes cold, warm, hot and mirrored alternate sites; section not re-read.

providerEquivalents.pattern: Provider backup service or customer-managed backup to a second location
providerEquivalents.note: Provider features found in discovery (playbook, RQ8).

basis.passage: Backup and restore (RPO in hours, RTO in 24 hours or less)
Tier 3: RTO ranging from hours to days and RPO measured in hours; backup and restore

rungs.name: Pilot light
rungs.plainName: Pilot light (data replicated, core services ready, compute started on failover)
rungs.definition: Data is replicated to the recovery location and core infrastructure is provisioned; application compute is not running and is started and scaled on failover.

providerEquivalents.note: AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery takes the pilot light approach with RPO in seconds and RTO in minutes; it is an option under DR-02 and DR-03, not DR-01 or DR-04.

providerEquivalents.pattern: Active-passive (cold standby): secondary infrastructure and replication ready, compute stopped
providerEquivalents.note: Azure's 'cold standby' is closer to AWS pilot light than to backup and restore: data replication and infrastructure as code are in place, compute is stopped.

providerEquivalents.pattern: Replication to a second region or site of the provider, compute on demand

basis.passage: Pilot light (RPO in minutes, RTO in tens of minutes)

rungs.name: Warm standby
rungs.plainName: Warm standby (a smaller copy always running)
rungs.definition: A scaled-down but fully functional copy runs in the recovery location with live replicated data; on failover it is scaled up.

providerEquivalents.note: Azure Tier 1 uses 'a mix of active-active or warm standby'.

providerEquivalents.pattern: Warm or hot site with running reduced capacity
Reduced-capacity standby in a second region or site

basis.passage: Warm standby (RPO in seconds, RTO in minutes)

rungs.name: Hot standby (active-passive at full capacity)
rungs.plainName: Hot standby (a full-size copy ready to take over)
rungs.definition: A full-capacity copy runs in the recovery location with live replicated data and automated or one-step failover; it does not serve production traffic until failover.

providerEquivalents.pattern: Hot standby (warm standby at full capacity)
providerEquivalents.note: AWS: 'When fully scaled this is known as hot standby'.

providerEquivalents.pattern: Active-passive warm standby scaled to full capacity with automatic failover
providerEquivalents.note: Azure has no separately named full-capacity active-passive pattern, and its glossary uses 'hot standby' for active-active. Terminology differs; the report names the pattern in words.

providerEquivalents.pattern: Full-capacity standby in a second region or site

basis.passage: The more scaled-up the warm standby is, the lower RTO and control plane reliance will be. When fully scales this is known as hot standby.

rungs.name: Multi-site active-active
rungs.plainName: Active-active (two or more sites serving live traffic)
rungs.definition: The service runs and serves traffic from two or more sites or regions at once, with data synchronised between them; a failed site is evacuated.

providerEquivalents.note: AWS: replication does not protect against data corruption or destruction unless point-in-time recovery is included.

basis.passage: Multi-Region (multi-site) active-active (RPO near zero, RTO potentially zero) ... should only be selected when business requirements necessitate it.
Warm standby RTO in minutes; hot standby lowers RTO further

basis.reasoning: Under 15 minutes leaves no time to scale a reduced standby reliably; a full-capacity standby is the lowest-cost pattern that meets it. Active-active is offered only as a business choice (businessChoices).

basis.passage: Warm standby RTO in minutes; pilot light RTO in tens of minutes

basis.reasoning: Pilot light may meet the upper half of the band, but 'tens of minutes' overlaps the 15-minute lower edge, so the lowest-cost pattern that meets the whole band is warm standby. The report shows pilot light as the alternative one rung down, with that risk stated.

basis.passage: Pilot light RTO in tens of minutes
Tier 2: RTO and RPO measured in hours; active-passive warm/cold

basis.reasoning: Backup and restore is stated as 'RTO in 24 hours or less', with no lower bound; restores at scale often take more than 4 hours, so DR-01 is not relied on below 4 hours.

basis.passage: Backup and restore (RTO in 24 hours or less)
Tier 3: RTO from hours to days; backup and restore
Backup and restore (RTO in 24 hours or less)
Warm standby (RPO in seconds)
Synchronous replication: changes are written to multiple locations simultaneously, ensuring zero data loss

basis.reasoning: Near-zero data loss needs continuous (and, for zero, synchronous) replication with a live target, which is DR-03 or above. It does not by itself need active-active (R9 decision 4, superseded by D3).

basis.passage: Warm standby (RPO in seconds); pilot light (RPO in minutes)

basis.reasoning: 'Minutes' for pilot light overlaps the 15-minute edge; warm standby is the lowest pattern that meets the whole band. AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery (pilot light approach, RPO in seconds) is a platform option inside this rung.

basis.passage: Pilot light (RPO in minutes)

basis.reasoning: Point-in-time recovery can bring backup and restore to as low as 5 minutes only 'in some cases', so DR-01 is not relied on below one hour.

basis.passage: Backup and restore (RPO in hours)
Backup and restore (RPO in hours)
Backup and restore (RPO in hours)

selection.description: Recommended rung = the higher-ranked of rung(effective RTO) and rung(effective RPO): the lowest-cost pattern that meets both. Effective values are the stated objectives after the consistency rules and any recorded requirement floor.
selection.whenUnknownDescription: If the effective RTO or RPO is Unknown or unanswered, no rung is issued for that service; finding RES.REQ.DEFINED (Critical) is raised. Never inferred from technology (validation row 33).
decisionLog: Rung for your recovery time objective: <rto answer> -> <rung> (<basis>)
Rung for your recovery point objective: <rpo answer> -> <rung> (<basis>)
Recommended: <rung>, the higher of the two
Requirement tightened by <floor id> (<regime> <article>) from <answer> to <answer>, if any
Requirement tightened by <consistency rule id> because <objective> exceeded <tolerance>, if any
Business choice offered: <offer> beside <recommended>, if any
Controls added by modifiers: <list>; no modifier changes the rung

businessChoices.why: Hot standby meets an RTO under 15 minutes with near-zero data loss. Active-active removes the failover step and serves traffic from both sites, at the highest cost and operational complexity; AWS says it should only be selected when business requirements necessitate it. The client decides; the report records the decision.

basis.passage: Multi-site active/active is the most operationally complex of the DR strategies, and should only be selected when business requirements necessitate it.
Tier 0: RTO measured in seconds and RPO approaching zero; an active-active, multi-region deployment is typically necessary

requirementConsistency.onConflict: If the stated RTO is longer than the impact tolerance (time), the ladder uses the impact tolerance band as the effective RTO.
requirementConsistency.finding: RES.REQ.CONSISTENT (High): the recovery time objective allows a longer outage than the service can tolerate.

basis.passage: 3.14: requirements might include recovery time objectives and recovery point objectives ... set to enable the firm to deliver the important business service within its impact tolerance
3.2: RTOs of the underlying business functions and their dependencies will meet the SRTOs

requirementConsistency.onConflict: If the stated RPO allows more data loss than the data-loss tolerance, the ladder uses the data-loss tolerance band as the effective RPO.
requirementConsistency.finding: RES.REQ.CONSISTENT (High): the recovery point objective allows more data loss than the service can tolerate.

basis.passage: 38(b): the maximum extent of data loss the entity would accept as a result of a disruption

requirementFloors.article: MAS TRM Notice for the licence type (for example Notice FSM-N09, para 6, finance companies: RTO of not more than 4 hours for each critical system)
requirementFloors.when: SG_MAS_TRM graded 'applies' (Sovereign IQ registry rule SG_MAS_TRM.1, fact ent.flags includes sg_mas_licensed) and the consultant confirms (REG-02 'mas_critical_system') that the service depends on a system the institution treats as a critical system under its TRM Notice.
requirementFloors.record: If EX-03 is '4-24 hours', '>24 hours' or longer than 4 hours, the effective RTO becomes '1-4 hours' and the decision log records the floor and article. The rung may rise as a result; the article is shown beside it.

basis.passage: 6: A finance company must establish a recovery time objective ('RTO') of not more than 4 hours for each critical system.
MAS requires critical systems to be restorable within four hours of an outage (MAS response, 19 Oct 2023)

basis.reasoning: The equivalent paragraph in the TRM Notices for banks, payment institutions and other licence types has not been re-read; RQ2 confirms each notice before the floor is shown for that licence type.

alwaysAdd.when: Always, for every service with a rung
alwaysAdd.finding: Raised only if DC-01 shows point-in-time restore is missing or untested (RES.BACKUP.PITR).

alwaysAdd.name: Continuous data replication for RPO under 15 minutes

basis.passage: Warm standby: Data is replicated and live in the recovery Region.
Synchronous replication ... ensuring zero data loss; asynchronous replication ... allowing for some data loss

modifiers.finding: G-05 Cyber recovery gap (Critical) when EX-08 is 'Yes' or 'Unknown'; High when isolated by design but not tested.

basis.passage: Art. 12(3): restore on ICT systems that are physically and logically segregated from the source ICT system
500.16(e): backups adequately protected from unauthorized alterations or destruction
at least one set of backups should be segregated from the network and offline

modifiers.when: EX-19 is 'No', 'Unknown' or 'Yes, documented, not tested'
modifiers.finding: G-06 Identity recovery gap: Critical for 'No' or 'Unknown'; High for documented but not tested.

modifiers.when: EX-11 is 'High concentration' or 'Unknown', or AF-DR-04 is 'Yes' or 'Unknown': correlation (G-04). EX-11 'Moderate concentration': concentration only (R9 decision 6).
modifiers.finding: G-04 Recovery-production correlation (Critical) for high or unknown; G-08 Third-party concentration (High) for moderate.

modifiers.when: EX-05 is not 'Yes, current and validated', or AF-DR-04 is 'Partially'

5.9: update their mapping annually at a minimum

modifiers.name: Critical third party without an alternative
modifiers.when: EX-10 is 'Yes, with no viable alternative' or 'Unknown'; or EXIT-01 is not 'Yes, partial migration or substitution rehearsed'

basis.passage: 56: ensure it can conduct an orderly exit from the arrangement if needed
Art. 28(8): exit plans shall be comprehensive, documented ... sufficiently tested and reviewed periodically

modifiers.name: SaaS data
modifiers.when: EX-18 includes 'SaaS' and SAAS-01 is not 'Yes, independent backup, restore tested'

basis.passage: Regardless of the type of deployment, you always retain ... Data: You're responsible for your data

invariants: Monotonic: a stricter RTO or RPO answer never yields a lower rung (checked over the full grid, RQ3 gate).
Modifiers, evidence, criticality, cyber exposure, concentration and environments never change the rung; they add controls and findings.
Only a recorded requirement floor or consistency rule changes the effective requirement, and the decision log names it with its article.
Unknown or unanswered RTO or RPO withholds the rung for that service; it is never inferred.
DR-05 is never the recommended rung; it is offered beside DR-04 only when RTO is under 15 minutes and RPO is near-zero.
